program:
:- prefix(ex, 'https://example.org/1428/').
ex:ans(X, D) :- X is 0, D is 6 / 2.
?- ex:ans(X, D).

provenance.derivation: 6/2 = 3 exactly, but the `/` operator is EXACT RATIONAL division and always commits a Value::Rat (never collapses back to Value::Int even when the quotient is a whole number) -- so the expected transport surface is the rational 3/1, not the integer 3. This is the ℚ-path distinguishing fact this case exercises. `X` is an unused dummy arg (`X is 0`) so the goal atom is arity >= 2, keeping the query on the binary backward path -- see the corpus README's arity note.
provenance.note: independently derived; never hand-edited to match the native engine
